scenes.title: 2007 Dallas 150-Foot Outdoor SCAD Tower Drop & Flashing LED Wrist Chronometer (Outdoor Iconic)
scenes.era: 2007, Outdoor 150-Foot SCAD Free-Fall Tower, Dallas, Texas

layout.description: Sunlit open-air 150-foot steel lattice SCAD drop tower rising above a wide blue-and-white suspended safety net in bright Texas daylight: an adult volunteer in a cobalt windbreaker and safety helmet hangs horizontally from an overhead release latch with left forearm raised in front of their eyes showing a glowing amber-red flickering LED wrist band, while David Eagleman stands on the steel platform holding the release lever.

positions.who: Free-fall volunteer (clothed 2.5D matte cream-white vinyl adult with smooth earless noseless hairless oval head and wide 2D charcoal-black ink eyes in cobalt windbreaker, harness, and helmet)
positions.where: suspended horizontally beneath the overhead steel drop arm 150 feet above the taut square catch net
positions.facing: facing skyward while staring intensely at the raised left-wrist LED chronometer

positions.who: Neuroscientist operator (clothed 2.5D matte cream-white vinyl adult in khaki field shirt and safety vest)
positions.where: standing on the railed upper steel tower deck beside the mechanical release latch
positions.facing: angled toward the suspended volunteer and the drop zone below

props.name: custom matte-black wrist perceptual chronometer with rapid-alternating LED square
props.period_detail: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) bespoke wrist LED display calibrated just above ground flicker fusion with zero readable text
props.physical_behavior: State-A: volunteer raises strapped wrist inches from wide ink eyes as the LED square shimmers in a solid amber blur -> State-B: overhead steel latch snaps open and the volunteer drops briskly downward while the wrist display remains an unreadable blur

props.name: overhead steel SCAD quick-release latch and giant taut square catch net far below
props.period_detail: authentic unattached backward free-fall tower rig documented in AP Archive SCAD footage
props.physical_behavior: State-A: steel hook holds back harness taut -> State-B: operator pulls lever, latch springs open, and volunteer plummets cleanly toward the cushioned net

actions.verb_sequence: volunteer holds flickering LED wrist strap steady before wide ink eyes -> operator pulls the steel release handle -> latch pops open and volunteer drops backward into open sky

reactions.reaction: 2D charcoal-black ink eyes snap wide with raised arched brows while trying in vain to resolve the blurred wrist glow
leans over the safety rail tracking the 2.5-second plunge with a handheld timer

scenes.wardrobe: Cobalt-blue athletic windbreaker, dark trousers, black safety harness, and white helmet; researcher in khaki button-down shirt.
scenes.lighting: Crisp bright outdoor midday Texas sunlight against open blue sky.
scenes.recognition_hook: Falling 150 feet backward at 70 miles per hour while staring at a flashing wristband — and discovering your eyes never sped up by even one percent!

key_visual.description: an adult volunteer in a cobalt windbreaker dropping backward from an outdoor steel tower crane above a wide catch net while staring at a glowing wrist chronometer

scenes.title: Ground-Deck Stopwatch Comparison: 2.5s Real Clock vs 36% Longer Memory Replay
scenes.era: 2007, Sunlit Ground Deck Beside the Dallas SCAD Safety Net

layout.description: Bright outdoor ground deck beside the cushioned SCAD net where the landed volunteer clicks a silver handheld stopwatch long after the researcher's reference timer has already stopped.

positions.who: Landed volunteer in cobalt windbreaker (helmet tucked under left arm)
positions.where: standing on the sunlit wooden deck clicking a brushed-silver stopwatch
positions.facing: facing the neuroscientist across a portable field table

positions.who: David Eagleman figure in khaki shirt
positions.where: standing opposite at the field table holding the wrist chronometer cradle

props.name: paired brushed-silver handheld stopwatches on portable field table
props.period_detail: measures watched-fall baseline (100%) vs own-fall retrospective duration (136%) with zero printed text
props.physical_behavior: State-A: both thumbs start timers together -> State-B: researcher clicks stop at 2.5 seconds while the jumper holds thumb down 36% longer before clicking

actions.verb_sequence: holds silver stopwatch thumb button down past the researcher's click -> presses stop late in surprise

reactions.reaction: blinks in disbelief realizing zero wrist numbers were readable despite the stretched memory

scenes.wardrobe: Cobalt windbreaker with helmet held at hip; khaki field shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: Your own fall feels 36 percent longer on the stopwatch afterward — even though your eyes missed every single flashing digit on the way down.

scenes.title: Everyday Kitchen Counter & Sunlit Tree-Lined Walk: Breaking Adult Autopilot
scenes.era: Modern sunlit neighborhood sidewalk & home kitchen

layout.description: Warm morning kitchen counter transitioning outdoors onto an unfamiliar sunlit autumn neighborhood street where a 50-year-old adult folds a paper map / closes phone and looks up at fresh architectural landmarks.

positions.who: 50-year-old adult walker (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl character in camel wool coat)
positions.where: striding briskly along a sunlit brick neighborhood walkway
positions.facing: turning head attentively toward fresh street trees and storefronts

props.name: pocketed dark smartphone and sunlit brick corner archway
props.period_detail: everyday adult application of Clewett, DuBrow & Davachi (2019) hippocampal event-boundary density
props.physical_behavior: State-A: walker slips silent phone into coat pocket -> State-B: steps onto a brand-new sunlit side street scanning fresh landmarks

actions.verb_sequence: slips phone cleanly into coat pocket -> turns onto a sunlit tree-lined avenue taking in fresh surroundings

reactions.reaction: relaxed bright ink expression as rich new hippocampal snapshots slow subjective decades down

scenes.wardrobe: Camel wool jacket, dark knit scarf, tailored trousers.
scenes.recognition_hook: Novelty writes dense hippocampal snapshots just like adrenaline — stretching your years without needing a crisis.
